input: Can u detect any anomaly which happended on june 2nd week
output:
I found the anomalies. Let me give you a clear picture of what happened during June's 2nd week (and early 3rd). Here's what the sweep surfaced:

## 🚨 The one real incident: **Fill rate drop (Jun 23–25)**

This is the standout — a genuine **technical break** with a concrete root cause:

- **Fill rate fell 4.4%** over **Jun 23–25** (−8.7 sigma, well past the detection gate).
- **Cause: `os_version = Android 15`** — fill rate collapsed **−8.56pp** on 10.3% of all traffic. (`iOS 17.2` also dipped −6.61pp on another 10.3%.)
- **Why it's a delivery fault, not a market event:** all 500 advertisers kept bidding, render rate held steady (0.979), eCPM held (2.348), and requests were actually *up* 4%. Both demand and supply were present — the *matching* step in the middle is what failed.
- **Cost: ~$4.97/day → about $14.91 total** while it ran.
- **Status: RECOVERED** on Jun 26 (back to 0.7854 vs. 0.7837 normal). No longer bleeding.
- **Owner:** Engineering. Point to look: the request→sale step, specific to Android 15 (every other OS version stayed normal — so it's not platform-wide).
- **Don't chase:** 39 segments that *looked* affected but were just dilution (e.g. `APAC|iOS 16.4`, `MEA|Pixel 7`, `LATAM|Android 14`, `AE|native`, `ES|interstitial`).

Priority: **post-mortem** — already recovered, so nothing to page on, but worth understanding so it doesn't recur (~$15 lost).

## 📉 Other windows that came up (ranked candidates, mostly not real)

- **Revenue drop Jun 15–22** (US|interstitial lead) — investigated, **no anomaly.** Moved only −7.4% at −2.7 sigma, and no segment cleared significance. Platform-level, nothing to route.
- **Requests dip Jun 21–22** (−22.9%) — investigated. **Recovered next day;** no segment responsible, uniform across everything (points to something shared by all traffic). Not localizable.
- **rpr/ecpm dip Jun 16–22** (app_00022) — **no anomaly** at platform level; segment didn't clear its own gate.
- **Revenue jump Jun 26–30** (app_00141 +54%) — **no anomaly**, within band (−0.4 sigma).
- **CTR spikes** (tier_1|Android 12 +70%, EU|iOS 17.2 +43%) — flagged, but both are small-window/small-sigma events.

**Bottom line:** The only thing that genuinely broke in that stretch was the **Android 15 fill-rate delivery fault on Jun 23–25** — already recovered, owned by Engineering, cost ~$15.

Want me to set up a watch so you get notified if the Android 15 fill-rate issue comes back? Or dig deeper into anything here (e.g. the revenue dip or the requests drop)?

I found the anomalies. Let me give you a clear picture of what happened during June's 2nd week (and early 3rd). Here's what the sweep surfaced:

## 🚨 The one real incident: **Fill rate drop (Jun 23–25)**

This is the standout — a genuine **technical break** with a concrete root cause:

- **Fill rate fell 4.4%** over **Jun 23–25** (−8.7 sigma, well past the detection gate).
- **Cause: `os_version = Android 15`** — fill rate collapsed **−8.56pp** on 10.3% of all traffic. (`iOS 17.2` also dipped −6.61pp on another 10.3%.)
- **Why it's a delivery fault, not a market event:** all 500 advertisers kept bidding, render rate held steady (0.979), eCPM held (2.348), and requests were actually *up* 4%. Both demand and supply were present — the *matching* step in the middle is what failed.
- **Cost: ~$4.97/day → about $14.91 total** while it ran.
- **Status: RECOVERED** on Jun 26 (back to 0.7854 vs. 0.7837 normal). No longer bleeding.
- **Owner:** Engineering. Point to look: the request→sale step, specific to Android 15 (every other OS version stayed normal — so it's not platform-wide).
- **Don't chase:** 39 segments that *looked* affected but were just dilution (e.g. `APAC|iOS 16.4`, `MEA|Pixel 7`, `LATAM|Android 14`, `AE|native`, `ES|interstitial`).

Priority: **post-mortem** — already recovered, so nothing to page on, but worth understanding so it doesn't recur (~$15 lost).

## 📉 Other windows that came up (ranked candidates, mostly not real)

- **Revenue drop Jun 15–22** (US|interstitial lead) — investigated, **no anomaly.** Moved only −7.4% at −2.7 sigma, and no segment cleared significance. Platform-level, nothing to route.
- **Requests dip Jun 21–22** (−22.9%) — investigated. **Recovered next day;** no segment responsible, uniform across everything (points to something shared by all traffic). Not localizable.
- **rpr/ecpm dip Jun 16–22** (app_00022) — **no anomaly** at platform level; segment didn't clear its own gate.
- **Revenue jump Jun 26–30** (app_00141 +54%) — **no anomaly**, within band (−0.4 sigma).
- **CTR spikes** (tier_1|Android 12 +70%, EU|iOS 17.2 +43%) — flagged, but both are small-window/small-sigma events.

**Bottom line:** The only thing that genuinely broke in that stretch was the **Android 15 fill-rate delivery fault on Jun 23–25** — already recovered, owned by Engineering, cost ~$15.

Want me to set up a watch so you get notified if the Android 15 fill-rate issue comes back? Or dig deeper into anything here (e.g. the revenue dip or the requests drop)?

## 🚨 The one real incident: **Fill rate drop (Jun 23–25)**

This is the standout — a genuine **technical break** with a concrete root cause:

- **Fill rate fell 4.4%** over **Jun 23–25** (−8.7 sigma, well past the detection gate).
- **Cause: `os_version = Android 15`** — fill rate collapsed **−8.56pp** on 10.3% of all traffic. (`iOS 17.2` also dipped −6.61pp on another 10.3%.)
- **Why it's a delivery fault, not a market event:** all 500 advertisers kept bidding, render rate held steady (0.979), eCPM held (2.348), and requests were actually *up* 4%. Both demand and supply were present — the *matching* step in the middle is what failed.
- **Cost: ~$4.97/day → about $14.91 total** while it ran.
- **Status: RECOVERED** on Jun 26 (back to 0.7854 vs. 0.7837 normal). No longer bleeding.
- **Owner:** Engineering. Point to look: the request→sale step, specific to Android 15 (every other OS version stayed normal — so it's not platform-wide).
- **Don't chase:** 39 segments that *looked* affected but were just dilution (e.g. `APAC|iOS 16.4`, `MEA|Pixel 7`, `LATAM|Android 14`, `AE|native`, `ES|interstitial`).

Priority: **post-mortem** — already recovered, so nothing to page on, but worth understanding so it doesn't recur (~$15 lost).

## 📉 Other windows that came up (ranked candidates, mostly not real)

- **Revenue drop Jun 15–22** (US|interstitial lead) — investigated, **no anomaly.** Moved only −7.4% at −2.7 sigma, and no segment cleared significance. Platform-level, nothing to route.
- **Requests dip Jun 21–22** (−22.9%) — investigated. **Recovered next day;** no segment responsible, uniform across everything (points to something shared by all traffic). Not localizable.
- **rpr/ecpm dip Jun 16–22** (app_00022) — **no anomaly** at platform level; segment didn't clear its own gate.
- **Revenue jump Jun 26–30** (app_00141 +54%) — **no anomaly**, within band (−0.4 sigma).
- **CTR spikes** (tier_1|Android 12 +70%, EU|iOS 17.2 +43%) — flagged, but both are small-window/small-sigma events.

**Bottom line:** The only thing that genuinely broke in that stretch was the **Android 15 fill-rate delivery fault on Jun 23–25** — already recovered, owned by Engineering, cost ~$15.
